title: How the UN Security Council Votes

segments.say: Of all the UN's bodies, only one can make decisions that every member must obey: the Security Council.
It has fifteen members: five permanent ones with a veto, and ten elected by the General Assembly for two years.
This is the chamber. To pass a resolution, nine of the fifteen must vote yes.
But on important matters, if any one of the five permanent members votes no, the resolution fails, even if all the others agree. That's the veto.

anim.title: The quiet exception
items: A permanent member can stay away

segments.say: Here's a detail examiners like: if a permanent member abstains instead of voting no, it's not a veto, and the resolution can still pass.

anim.title: India and the Council
items: Seeks a permanent seat and Council reform

segments.say: India has been an elected member eight times, most recently in twenty twenty-one and twenty-two, and argues for reform and a permanent seat.
For GS Two: fifteen members, nine votes to pass, a permanent 'no' is a veto, but an abstention is not.

sources: Charter of the United Nations, Articles 23 (composition: 5 permanent, 10 non-permanent elected for two years), 25 (members agree to carry out Council decisions) and 27 (nine affirmative votes; for non-procedural matters including the concurring votes of the permanent members)
United Nations, 'Voting system' (un.org/securitycouncil): abstention by a permanent member does not prevent adoption
Ministry of External Affairs: India's eighth term as non-permanent member, 2021–22; position on Council reform

quiz.q: How many votes does a Security Council resolution need?
quiz.why: Nine of fifteen, with no permanent member voting no on substantive matters.

quiz.q: A permanent member abstains. What happens?
How long is an elected member's term?
quiz.why: Ten members are elected for two years.

reviewNote: Facts were read against the UN Charter (Articles 23, 25, 27), the UN's page on voting, and MEA. Pictures show the building and an empty chamber. Moving facts: India's terms; reform talks.
